# Welcome and Introduction {#welcome-and-introduction}

Welcome to the Musculoskeletal Imaging and Intervention fellowship at the University of Wisconsin-Madison\! Fellowship can be one of the most rewarding years of your training. When you leave here, you will be ready to perform all aspects of musculoskeletal radiology both diagnostic and procedural. The first couple of months can be tough as you get your feet on the ground, but once you’re up and running you won’t believe how quickly the year will fly by\!

# Daily Workflow {#daily-workflow}

You can find the full clinical schedule at [https://www.radiology.wisc.edu](https://www.radiology.wisc.edu) \>  
Intranet \> Schedules \> Clinical Schedule or download the Qgenda App for your phone. You will rotate through 6 different clinical services:

* [Procedures at University Hospital (UH)](#procedures-at-uh-am/pm-\(g3/346\))  
* [Float at UH](#heading=h.2s8eyo1)  
* [Sports/Spine at UH](#sports/spine-at-uh-am/pm-\(mfcb-turski-education-center---tec\))  
* [ED/Bone at UH](#heading=h.tyjcwt)  
* [East Madison Hospital (EMH)](#east-madison-hospital-\(emh\))  
* [Science Drive Medical Center (SMC)](#science-drive-medical-center-\(smc\))

Each one of these is described in detail below. Over the course of the year, you’ll roughly spend an equal amount of time on each service. The schedule may vary but we try to have you on the same service for most of the week to settle in, especially in the first part of the year. 

Each service has its core responsibilities but ultimately the MSK section uses a shared work list. The expectation is that regardless of your assignment, everyone stays to help finish the list until all of the studies completed (marked as reviewed) before **4:30 PM** are read out. The volume and demands of each service vary but the most important thing is to have everyone pitching in to help out, especially as it gets towards the end of the day. **Keep an eye on the “MSK All” list throughout the day regardless of your service assignment so that you can help out as needed.** 

# Communication Expectations {#communication-expectations}

* Check your uwhealth.org email at least twice a day during the week. This is where most communication from the section will appear.   
* Check your wisc.edu email at least once a week. Various mandatory trainings and HR communications will get sent to this address.   
* Always notify your faculty the day before if you will be arriving late to service. For example if you have journal club or another off-site morning conference.  
* Notify faculty as far in advance as possible if you’ll be absent from a clinical service and be sure to follow the [time off request policy](#fellow-scheduling-and-time-off-requests) outlined on page 16\.  
* If calling in a sick day, please notify the clinical team, fellowship director, section chief and administrative assistant

# Clinical Rotations {#clinical-rotations}

## **Procedures at UH AM/PM (G3/346)** {#procedures-at-uh-am/pm-(g3/346)}

The basics:

* **Arrive:** In time to have all procedures pulled up on PACs (usually by **7:15-7:30a**) and ready to preview with the attending by 7:30a.   
* **First thing:** Pull up procedures on PACS, be ready to run the list.  
* **Primary role:** Procedures, reviewing procedure requests (green sheets)  
* **Secondary role:** Help out with dictating radiographs as much as possible. Goal is to read up to 20 or more radiographs per whole day shift.

The details:

The procedures rotation will allow you to develop expertise in a wide variety of image-guided MSK interventional procedures including spine interventions such as epidural, transforaminal, and facet injections; vertebroplasties, biopsies, and disc aspirations; joint injections and aspirations; CT- and US-guided soft tissue and bone biopsies; and image guided tumor ablations. The fellows play a pivotal role in managing the procedures service.

**Main responsibilities:**

1. Review the procedures *at least* the day before. Print the schedule from Health Link and make notes for each procedure directly on it. Discuss uncertain cases with the faculty and make phone calls/e-communication as necessary to resolve issues in advance that would be hard to solve on the day of the procedure. Review should include the following:  
   1. Procedure order and any comments.  
   2. Recent clinical note from the ordering provider (sometimes the procedure order does not reflect what they want; for example, right vs. left, steroid vs. anesthetic only, correct spine level, etc.).  
   3. Patient’s previous imaging. Use this to plan your approach.  
   4. Previous procedure notes if this is a repeat. Sometimes there will be notes in the dictation regarding tips for set up, needle gauge and length, patient anxiety   
   5. **Allergies**, medications, significant comorbidities  
   6. Transitional spinal anatomy and numbering.  
2. Show up around 7:15 AM and pull up all the morning cases.  
3. 7:30-7:45 AM – go over cases with the faculty (“run the list”)  
4. 7:55 AM – the tech usually gets the patient from the main waiting room and brings them back into the consenting/consult room. **Be proactive to help the day run on time.**  
5. You then enter the consult room, explain the procedure, answer questions, and then obtain written consent (ipad). Verify the patient’s allergies, medications if relevant (such as blood thinners) and that they are not on antibiotics or have some concurrent infection that would contraindicate the procedure. Record the patient’s pre-procedure pain score on the [pain reporting sheet](#bookmark=id.4i7ojhp).   
6. Escort the patient into the procedure room (MP1) and perform a TIMEOUT with the tech and patient all in the same room. Let the tech know what position you want the patient and then help them get the patient on the table.   
7. You will set the procedure up, typically with help from faculty early in the year and then independently as the year goes on. The faster you get accustomed to the fluoro table controls (practice\!\!) the easier time you will have with each subsequent procedure.  
8. Perform the procedure. Faculty must be in attendance from the point at which the procedure **needle enters the skin until the needle is removed**. This is very important to follow for compliance, liability and reimbursement reasons. Note that fellows are not credentialed to perform spine injections independently at our hospital (though they can do joint and US injections unsupervised).  
9. After the procedure, help the patient off the table and verify that they are doing okay. **Both you and the technologist should closely supervise the patient** until it is clear that they are doing well as vasovagal symptoms are not uncommon. Some patients will also report leg weakness. Have a low threshold to have the patient leave the department in a wheelchair. Record the post-procedure pain score and provide them with instructions on the [pain reporting sheet.](#bookmark=id.4i7ojhp)   
10. You are responsible for clearing all needles from the procedure tray. Keep an eye out for what you can do to help with turn around time and keep the room moving.  
11. The tech will help the patient back to the waiting room. Make a note of your fluoro time and pre- and post-injection pain scores for the dictation and get ready for the next procedure after you dictate your case.  
12. Important: Dictate your procedure before starting the next case. If you are using templates this can take less than a minute.

Additional responsibilities:

1. For procedures requiring conscious sedation (vertebroplasties, bone biopsies, ablations), there are some additional steps:  
   1. The night before you will need to place pre-procedure orders for the patient’s pre-admission to the 10-bed unit. The MSK Nurse (Erica Timm) can help you with this if needed. 263-6871, pager 9585  
   2. The morning of the procedure, you will go see the patient in the 10-bed pre- and post-procedure area to obtain consent and perform a focused history and physical exam.  
   3. Prior to the procedure, you will need to document the H\&P in Health Link and also document a separate attestation note indicating that you have evaluated them prior to sedation. Someone can show you how to do this the first time you run through it.   
   4. After the procedure, patients will return to 10-bed for recovery. You will need to place post-procedure orders for them immediately after the procedure. There are order sets available for this in HL.  
   5. If for biopsy you will need to place surgical pathology orders.  
        
2. When dictating each case, it is **your responsibility** to assure that all images from the case have made it to PACS.  Close the case as dictated when you are finished.  
3. Dictate all cases that you perform (after each case).  Use the default template that will pop up when you dictate but add in any specific details or considerations if needed, for example if the procedure was changed to a different site for technical reasons, changes were made to accommodate patient allergies, etc.  
4. Advanced procedure screening evaluation: you will get a green sheet from a scheduler or the MSK Clinical Program Coordinator (MSK Nurse Erica Timm) to evaluate a request for biopsy, vertebroplasty, or image-guided ablation.  Research the case and then discuss it with faculty to see if it’s a case we’ll do.  If the procedure is not indicated then **communication** with the referring service is vitally important. Please communicate with the provider and explain why we are not doing the procedure and also document a quick note in Health Link.  If approved, return the sheet to the MSK CPC.   
5. Remember, after any case with Anesthesiology, the fellow or faculty **must** accompany the patient back to Recovery.  
6. Occasionally you will be asked to see an inpatient on the floor for consent for a biopsy, plasty, etc.   
7. You should keep track of your advanced procedures so that you can present them at our every other month [Vertebroplasty conference](#bookmark=id.3rdcrjn). Dr. Ross will email you to get your cases.  
8. Acrylic Box in the Procedure RR. We get faxed forms for patients of outside providers that are scheduled for injections with us. They show up in the acrylic box on the wall.   
   1. As a fellow you need to:  
      1. Confirm that the ordering info in the faxed sheets matches what is on the schedule and write that on the sheet and return to Erica Timm. These are cases for all 3 of our sites (UH, EMH, SMC). She will update the health link schedule with notes indicating it was confirmed by you.

Radiology Residents on Procedures:  
There are times throughout the year, mostly at the end of the year, when a resident will rotate through the procedure rotation. It’s expected to integrate them as follows: show them how to prepare and run the list for the day, let them observe you consent a patient, show them how to do a procedure and then gradually give them more responsibility. Probably after a few days during the first week, start alternating procedures. Of course, you get priority of which procedures you’d like to do. Of note, during the last week or two of procedures, residents may fly solo. This will give you more academic time. Lastly, the resident will be doing float their last week of the procedure rotation to get that exposure to advanced MSK procedures.

**Float at UH AM G3/346**

The basics:

* The same as procedures but see details below. 

The details:

Start time/logistics: The procedure float rotation runs on Tuesday AM and every other Friday AM. Similar to the regular procedures rotation, you should arrive in time to have the cases pulled up and ready to go over with the attending at 7:30a. With the advanced cases requiring sedation on Float, you’ll need to arrive in plenty of time to get all the prep work done for an on-time first case start time of 8:00a, which includes consenting the patient in 10-bed.

Main responsibilities:   
The workflow is very similar to that of the Procedures rotation. Check the MSK float schedule for the cases that are assigned to you. Typically this will be biopsies, CT guided injections, ablations and vertebroplasty cases; because we have the CT fluoro scanner that morning, some SI joint injections may show up also. You will be responsible for working up the advanced cases ahead of time, putting in orders the day before for cases requiring conscious sedation, performing the targeted H\&P and attestation note the morning of the procedure for sedation cases, and getting written consent from all patients. You’ll do the case with the faculty and dictate the procedure immediately afterwards. Keep track of advanced cases and outcomes for presentation at our Vertebroplasty conference.

## **Sports/Spine at UH AM/PM (MFCB Turski Education Center \- TEC)** {#sports/spine-at-uh-am/pm-(mfcb-turski-education-center---tec)}

The basics:

* **Arrive:** No later than **7:30a,** earlier is better, especially early in the year.  
* **First thing:** Start dictating MRs to be ready for first read out when the attending arrives (\~5 MRIs at the start and \~7 second half of year). Over-read any after hours ultrasound (uncommon). Dictate overnight radiographs if no ED/Bone coverage or list is long.  
* **Primary role:** Joint and spine MRI assigned to MSK OP MR & CT read list. Protocoling MSK joint MRI and CT studies.  
* **Secondary role:** Help out with dictating radiographs as much as possible.

The details:

The Sports/Spine rotation focuses on MRI and CT of extremities and spine with interpretation of outpatient MRI and CTs performed across the system.

Main responsibilities

1. Your main responsibility is the MSK OP MR & CT list. Begin reviewing exams from oldest to newest. No cherry picking of cases and this expectation extends to rotating residents and MR fellows as well. Because you are running the rotation, feel free to manage the cases with the other rotating residents and MR fellows.   
2. MSK fellows assigned to other rotations (SMC, EMH, ED Bone, Procedures) are encouraged to take spine MRI and CTs. 	  
   1. EMH team should read at least 10 outpatient cross-sectionals  
   2. SMC team at least 5 outpatient cross sectionals  
3. ED or Inpatient MSK US: Watch out for occasional overnight ED, daytime ED, or inpatient MSK US cases (\~2/month) on the MSK ALL list. These should be expeditiously read out in the morning by the Sports/Spine team in case a non-MSK sonographer scanned the case and you need a repeat exam or more images.  
4. Fluoro cases: Each afternoon there may be added on inpatient or occasional outpatient joint injections or US aspirations that you will be asked to cover. The ED Bone team is first line for these but the Sports/Spine team may need to jump in at times.   
5. Protocol all cross-sectional cases (best to do them in batches throughout the workday) via the “MSK PWL”. Check with staff if you’re not certain which protocol to use. Look closely at the indication listed on the request but use more information from the EMR if the indication is not clear on the request. The Sports/Spine team is responsible for the “MSK PROTOCOL” worklist on Epic/Radiant which has the joint MR and CTs.  
6. After the radiology resident arrives in the morning, share the MR and CT cases with them.   
7. When the MR and CT scans have been read and all protocoling is up-to-date, start working your way down the [responsibility list.](#bookmark=id.vx1227)    
8. During the last 6 months of the fellowship, an abdominal or MR fellow often will be assigned to Sports/Spine.  On those days, you should share the CT and MR scans with them.  
9. Fellow teaching of residents is a priority. Take time to call the resident over to review an interesting or classic case. Encourage them to ask questions about their studies so they feel prepared for read out with the attending. Who knows, you might be voted Best Fellow Teacher of the Year\!

Additional duties:

1. Please note that all pediatric cases referred from AFCH (American Family Children’s Hospital) or small satellite clinics are protocoled and read by Pediatric Radiology. However, pediatric cases from the SMC and EMH Sports and Spine Clinics and from Dr. Hennessey (tumor surgeon) belong to MSK as well as cases generated from Sports Medicine (Drs. John Wilson, David Bernhardt, Kathleen Carr, Margaret Alison Brooks, Andrew Watson, Erin Hammer).  
2. Many MSK fellows have found it useful to quickly review the MR cases that they aren’t reading out and then listen when the faculty goes over them with the radiology resident or abdominal/MR fellow.  
3. Outpatient Spine CT and MRI are shared with Neuroradiology. Consult the [spine workflow](#bookmark=id.1v1yuxt) for more information. In general, we read all Ortho spine, Rehab Spine, family medicine, and outside providers. Neuroradiology will read all Neurology, Oncology, Neurosurgery, and internal medicine. Please don’t hesitate to ask.

**ED Bone at UH AM/PM (MFCB TEC)**

The basics:

* **Arrive:** No later than **7:30a**.  
* **First thing:** Over-read the overnight ED radiographs. Call the ED with any discrepancies per [Department policy.](#appendix-a:-managing-discrepancies-between-preliminary-and-final-radiology-report)   
* **Primary role:** Dictate radiographs, beginning with inpatients and then all outpt radiographs. Teach the Bone 1 resident (s) if on service. Respond to phone calls, OR spine reads, and WebEx queries. We have a reading room assistant (Heather Elvord) that can help contact people for you.  
* **Secondary role:** Help out with dictating all radiographs as much as possible.

The details:

The ED Bone rotation is a chance for fellows to work independently in the role of attending, covering the ED radiographs and the rest of the radiograph list. You will be assigned to this rotation 1-2 times per month starting in mid-July. Fellows have found this to be a useful rotation for gaining speed and confidence as they progress through this final year of training. Past fellows have said their comfort level rises as you progress throughout the year. Please also keep in mind that the **first year residents (Bone 1\)** are rotating through the ED Bone rotation. Their primary responsibility is the ED radiographs, followed by all other MSK radiographs. They will be given a reference on the Language of Fractures and Helm’s Fundamentals of Skeletal Radiology. You will also read out their studies as attending (avg. 10- 20 cases/shift) and teach them the basics of MSK ER radiology.

Start time/logistics: The ED Bone AM/PM shifts run from **7:30-12:30** or **12:30-4:30p** respectively. You will work out of the front room of the TEC. On some days, the ED shift may be a full day (730a to 430p). Past fellows have said they preferred a whole day shift over a half day shift. You will receive an extra stipend for covering this rotation.

Main responsibilities:

1. In the morning you will over-read any ED radiographs from the previous night that have been prelim’d by the resident. These will be indicated by a red exclamation point on the left hand side of the patient name. If you open the case and hit the dictate button it will pull up the resident’s report and allow you to approve it as-is or with any changes that you make**. If you make changes, you must refer to the department’s policy on [discrepancies](#appendix-a:-managing-discrepancies-between-preliminary-and-final-radiology-report) to be sure that you document and notify appropriately\! If an inpatient, you must call the admitting service.**   
2. During the shift you will give priority to ED radiographs. At this time, our section is only reading bone radiographs from the ED. Chest radiographs are read by the chest section; VP shunt series and soft tissue necks are read by neuro; and abdominal radiographs by Abdominal. Please reassign these cases if they are placed on our read list by accident.  
3. Our goal is a turn-around time of less than 1 hour for all ED studies (includes prelims). You cannot dictate a report on a study until it has been approved by the tech with an “OK” icon next to it in PACS. You can type a quick prelim into the “Blank Form” sheet in PACS prior to that. Even if you dictate the study and call the ED you should cut and paste your impression into the “Blank Form” space in PACS where it is most readily available for review by ED staff. This will become more apparent when you do it once or twice.  
4. **OR Spines:** You will receive occasional calls from techs in the OR for intraoperative spine localization radiographs (starting at 7:30 am). Confirm intraoperative needle localization for spine procedures with the surgeon by phone and dictate that you confirmed the localization at a specific time with the Dr. “surgeon name” who agreed with the localization. If no phone call then you can simply dictate the level and sign the report. ED/Bone is first line for responding to OR spine calls. The techs will then call the other reading rooms in order until they find either an attending or fellow to take the call.   
5. Though you are working independently, you should **feel free** to show any problematic cases to a faculty member, typically whomever is on Sports/Spine. It is expected and appropriate that you will ask for help as needed when working independently on ED/Bone\!  
6. When you are caught up on the ED radiographs, work your way through the radiograph list per the RR [responsibilities list](#bookmark=id.vx1227).

Additional duties:

1. You will likely receive many phone calls during your ED/Bone shift. This can be a frustrating distraction as you try to keep up with a busy radiograph list but it is the culture in our section that we try to provide assistance to whomever is calling whenever possible rather than divert them to someone else. Typical phone calls include:  
   1. A clinician calling for a result on a radiograph. This is a challenge as the study may be opened by someone in another reading room but not yet dictated. The way we have agreed to handle this is to go ahead and open up the exam and give the clinician a verbal report over the phone, then call whomever has the study open and let them know what you told the clinician so that they can contact them to follow up if they disagree. If no one else has the study open, then you can simply dictate it yourself and include that you discussed the results with the clinician. Please do not punt the caller to another reading room.  
   2. A tech calling or via Webex for a protocol for an inpatient or add-on CT or MRI. Please put in the protocol for them when they call. If it is early in the year and you need help, call the Sports/Spine team.  
   3. A scheduler calling or via WebEx with a question about an order or a procedure. Early in the year you may find these hard to answer on your own. Please take their contact number, confer with a faculty member, and call them back with your response. Later on you will find these questions easy to answer and the schedulers are very appreciative when we are able to help them out.   
   4. A call from a tech to check images. (MRI under anesthesia, check prior to contrast, check FOV, adequate coverage of pathology, no motion, good fat saturation, etc). Open up the exam and if you feel comfortable then provide the technologist the feedback they need to complete the protocol. This gets easier to do with confidence gained throughout the year and, again, it is okay to ask for help from faculty when needed.  
   5. ED/Bone often has the most telephone queries but these criteria apply broadly wherever you are rotating. It is an important part of our section’s culture that we are able to help people quickly when they contact us and the fellows play a larger role in this than anyone else.  
   6. A call from the MRI nurse (only at UH) to consent patients if they have a pacemaker. You have to walk to the MRI nursing area to directly consent the patient, not by phone.

## **East Madison Hospital (EMH)** {#east-madison-hospital-(emh)}

The basics:

* **Arrive:** No later than **7:30a**.  
* **First thing:** Pull up and preview all overnight ED and INPT cross-sectional cases (any location). If Bone 2 resident on then please share 1-2 overnight joints. Spines need to be read right away.  
* **Primary role:** ED/Inpatient MRI and CT. Surgical planning CTs. EMH radiographs. Protocol spine studies.  
* **Secondary role:** Help out with dictating radiographs as much as possible. Help with Sports/Spine list throughout the day. Should be picking up at least 10 outpatient MRI/CT to help decompress the list.  
* **Before leaving for the day:** Check with the MRI and CT techs to make sure contrast studies are all done. Otherwise, you need to stay to help cover contrast reactions up to 430p.

The details:

East Madison Hospital opened in August 2015\. It focuses on orthopedics, spine, and sports medicine but has a full emergency room, operating suites, and 56 inpatient beds. Radiology operates MR, CT, fluoroscopy, ultrasound and x-ray facilities at EMH.

Start time/logistics: The fellow should arrive in the second floor reading room at EMH by **7:30a.** If there is a Good Case Conference, you will need to arrive earlier in order to get logged into WebEx in time to join the conference remotely by 7:15 AM. There is both an upstairs and downstairs reading room at EMH. EMH US is also on the second floor. The PAs (Deb Trieloff, Ryan Schuett, Dan Hammes) are in the first floor RR. They cover the fluoro joint injections. We read from the second floor reading room everyday except Tuesdays when we read from the downstairs reading room as all of the ultrasound cases are downstairs on Tuesdays.

Main responsibilities:

1. The day before, check the schedule of US procedures at EMH and spot any problems. In the morning, you will run the US list (typically 7-8 cases/day) with the sonographer and go over any issues that either of you have identified.  
2. You will cover all of the MSK US cases (diagnostic and procedures) performed at EMH. EMH US will be on the second floor near the reading room.  
3. All fluoro-guided procedures are covered by the PAs. At times, they will call you for help in planning, positioning, or trouble shooting. **You are welcome to participate in any procedure you want to try out or want more experience with, especially small joints.** All faculty are aware of this opportunity and more than happy to cover other cases in the meantime. There may also be an US-guided biopsy to be performed by the fellow. You should interpret any MR arthrograms for which you did the injection.  
4. The team at EMH bears the primary responsibility for ED and INPT studies. In the morning, this may include ED and INPT studies that were prelim’d by the resident the night before. **Once again, any changes that are made need to be documented according to the department policy on [discrepancies.](#appendix-a:-managing-discrepancies-between-preliminary-and-final-radiology-report)** Additionally, for weeks when MSK is doing emergency spine imaging, any spine exam read by the resident as normal needs to be signed off by the faculty by 9:00 AM. The fellow should help facilitate this process. You will continue to interpret the ED/inpatient cross sectional studies as they come across throughout the day. Please share 1-2 overnight joint studies with the Bone 2 resident who arrives at 830a. Keep track of good call cases from overnight and show them to the Bone 2 resident on service to help with their learning.   
5. The EMH team is responsible for protocoling all MSK Spine studies. This should be done in batches during the day to keep the list cleared. Refer to the [spine workflow](#bookmark=id.1v1yuxt) as needed if you’re not sure if the case should go to neuroradiology.   
6. We started an EMH Spine procedures service in early 2019 – every Wed in the 1st floor fluoro room. The EMH spine rotation is typically covered by an MSK faculty without a fellow or resident. Occasionally, a fellow will also be assigned. So on Wed, the fluoro joint procedures will be performed in a separate room by the PA with a C-arm across the hall from CT.

Additional duties:

7. There may be a Bone 2 resident on service as well. Usually they are at UH but sometimes at EMH. You should share the work-list with them and particularly encourage them to grab the ED studies whenever possible so that they can build their experience for call. Residents are not available during conference times, 730-815a and 12-1p so be sure to cover the ED studies then.   
8. The MRI and CT technologists will often call or Webex for help with protocols or to check images. Please help them out as best you can. Both the MRI and CT scanners are very close to the downstairs reading room and this is an excellent time to go directly to the scanner when a question arises. The technologists are always very happy to get some face time with the rads\!

## **Science Drive Medical Center (SMC)** {#science-drive-medical-center-(smc)}

The basics:

* **Arrive:** By **7:30a** to be ready to run the list with the sonographers/attending  
* **First thing:** Run the list with the sonographers and the attending. Help with overnight radiographs as needed.  
* **Primary role:** Scheduled ultrasound and fluoro cases.  
* **Secondary role:** Help out with dictating radiographs as much as possible. Help with spine MRI. Read MR arthrograms that you injected. SMC team should pick up at least 5 outpatient MRI/CT from the Sports Spine list throughout the day to help decompress the list.  
* **Before leaving for the day:** Check with the MRI techs to make sure contrast studies are all done. Otherwise, you need to stay to help cover contrast reactions. These are often done by 4:30 and rarely later than 5:00pm.

The details:

Start time/logistics: Arrive by 7:30am to give you time to check in with the sonographers and run the list before the day gets started. If you are away for a mandatory conference on an SMC day, please **alert** your faculty ahead of time so she/he will know to show up early to cover. In general, aim to email faculty prior to 4pm the day before as not all faculty check email after work hours.

Main responsibilities:

1. Musculoskeletal ultrasound (MSK US) scans and US-guided injections are done in two rooms at SMC all day, 5 days a week.  The schedule starts at 0810 in SMC US room 1 and 0740 in SMC US room 2\. You should expect to gain hands-on experience by scanning as much as possible. You will need to be proactive with getting hands-on scanning time since this will be the only way to learn MSK US. I cannot emphasize this point enough. The sonographers are typically very willing to help you learn although they need to keep the day moving along so their schedule doesn’t get behind. We have enough time built into the schedule to allow for fellow scanning.  
2. Run the list by reviewing all cases for the day with each sonographer prior to starting the day. They are supposed to come to the reading room to quickly go over the list to make sure everyone is on the same page.   
3. Urgent cases may be added from Sports Medicine Clinic. Add-on slots change frequently but are often available. You should check and confirm with the sonographer.   
4. Assist with radiographs and spine MRI according to the responsibility list.   
5. Radiology residents will rotate through the service some months. Split the procedures with them and make sure they’re involved with the interesting diagnostic cases.   
6. One Sports medicine fellow will rotate throughout the year (2-3 half days a month) and should be incorporated into the rotation as much as possible. Ortho interns will also spend a few days in the US reading room and should be involved in discussions. The sports fellows are more likely to take an active interest in scanning.  
7. You and the resident will cover the fluoro injections during the day as well (don’t give the resident more than two injections). You should interpret any MR arthrograms for which you did the injection. On Fridays, one of our PAs (usually Ryan Schuett) will cover all fluoro injections.  
8. While these duties are being completed, including dictating all your cases, you can work your way through the [list of responsibilities,](#bookmark=id.vx1227) converging on “MSK All” as on the other services.  
9. All fellows will have the opportunity for dedicated hands-on training in a 1-day MSK US course held at the UW School of Sonographer in October on a Friday block. Dates TBD.

#  Teaching Conferences {#teaching-conferences}

These conferences are mandatory. Attendance is via WebEx with the meeting link on your Outlook calendar. 

1. MSK Good Case Conference:   
   1. When: weekly at 7:15-8:00 AM, please check the daily schedule. Usually Thursdays.  
   2. What: A chance for fellows and faculty to show and discuss interesting cases. Bring one or two cases to share each week. Low key, don’t over prepare.  
        
2. Vertebroplasty Conference (M\&M):  
   1. When: Every other month, Thursday mornings instead of GCC, dates vary, check the schedule  
   2. What: Coordinated by Dr. Ross. Fellows present advanced cases (vertebroplasties, biopsies, ablations) for review, final pathology if applicable, and discussion.  
        
3. Journal Club: (in person)  
   1. When: Monday at 7AM, \~5x per year.  
   2. What: Coordinated by Dr. Blankenbaker. Run by a different attending each time. They will provide several papers to read about 1 week ahead of time for discussion. (Free breakfast\!)  
        
4. Scope Correlation Conference:  
   1. When: Thursdays (instead of GCC) at 7:15 AM, 3x per year  
   2. What: Coordinated by Dr. Tang. Fellows take turns running scope correlation conferences on a particular theme (e.g. knee-meniscus, shoulder labrum, hip labrum).   
        
5. Sarcoma Conference: (encouraged but mandatory only if presenting)  
   1. When: Biweekly on Fridays, 7:00-8:00 AM   
   2. What: Representatives from Rad-MSK, Ortho tumor, Oncology, Radiation Oncology and/or Pathology gather to discuss cases.   
   3. Fellows will take turns presenting at this tumor board   
6. Rheumatology conference:   
   1. When: Thursday 7:30-8:30 AM, bimonthly.  
   2. What: Fellow assigned to present with assistance of assigned faculty. Cases provided by rheumatology with specific questions should be no later than the Friday before the scheduled conference. A short PPT on a specific teaching topic is created. These are reused and edited/improved by the fellows each year.  
        
7. Ortho tumor conference:   
   1. When: Second Tuesday of the month 6:30-7:15 AM.  
   2. What: Radiology presented by Dr. Symanski. Tumor cases presented by ortho resident. Ortho runs this conference via Bluejeans. Ortho will send you the link.  
   3. Fellows are expected to attend ortho tumor conference. These can be attended remotely via the Zoom.

8. Bone Pathology conference:   
   1. When: Wednesday 7:30 AM, bimonthly, check schedule.  
   2. What: Fellow selected to present imaging findings with pathologic correlation. Faculty is assigned to help the fellow. Find time to review the cases with them prior to the conference. If there’s an interesting case you would like to include in the conference please email Dr. Darya Buehler in Pathology. They are eager to receive cases from Radiology\!

9. Radiology-Orthopedics Seminar (Rad-Ortho):  
   1. When: \~Quarterly in place of GCC  
   2. What: About once per quarter we invite an orthopedic surgery attending to present at our conference as a chance to hear from them on a topic and discuss cases together.   
        
10. Resident MSK Lectures (encouraged but optional):  
    1. When: Either 7:30-8:15 AM or 12pm-1pm  
    2. Case Conferences and Lectures occur a few times a month. These can be very helpful for fellows. You can listen to the conference on WebEx. Faculty are ok with you attending these lectures but please give them a heads up so they can help cover the service. Pro tip: these are recorded and can be viewed asynchronously.  
         
11. Optional:  
    1. Weekly 7:00 AM Sports med conferences  
    2. However, 3 or 4 of these are correlation conferences with one radiology attending and one sports attending.  
    3. Ortho Grand Rounds: Weds 7:15 AM 

       

MSK Administrative Assistant, Natalie Roisum or Nicole Howard, will send you a meeting invite from the “**Radiology-MSK Calendar – DOR”** to post all of these seminars and conferences listed above to your own UWHealth.org Outlook Calendar.  The conference schedule will also show on Qgenda but Outlook will have the WebEx link.   
[https://www.radiology.wisc.edu/protected/intranet/schedules/index.php](https://www.radiology.wisc.edu/protected/intranet/schedules/index.php)

# Taking Call {#taking-call}

1. **Call week:** Fellows share the call with faculty. Your first week on call, you will be on back up and the attending will be primary. This is your opportunity to get oriented by the faculty to the on-call environment. Check with your faculty on how they want to handle this. Each call week begins on Monday (or Tuesday if Monday is a holiday) at 7:30 AM and ends the following Monday (or Tuesday if a Monday is a holiday) at 7:30 AM. While you are on call, the radiology resident on call may contact you for questions on MSK imaging or to come in for MSK joint aspirations. You nor the faculty receive extra pay since this is part of the fellowship training.   
2. **Daytime on Saturday, Sunday and Holidays:**  You will come in by 7:30 AM to review the overnight studies and read out the senior overnight resident around 8:00 AM. Usually it’s best to check in with them when you arrive and have them come find you in the procedures reading room (G3/346) to read out when they are ready. At 9:00 AM you will read out with the junior resident. This is done remotely over phone/Webex as they often only have a few studies left from the day before. Nonetheless, it’s important to read out both residents for teaching purposes, even in abbreviated fashion, consistently every weekend morning. **Please reach out to them proactively to ensure that read outs happen.**  Afterwards (and possibly before), read out all MSK radiographs, inpatient CTs and inpatient MRIs on the “MSK ALL list”. You do not need to read late outpatient MR scans from SMC, EMH, and 1SP from Friday evening. Likewise outpatient MRIs done over the weekend at any site can wait until Monday morning. MSK reads out all spine CTs and spine MRIs ordered by the ER and inpatients on Ortho spine surgery weeks according to the schedule posted on the webpage, as long as a head/maxillofacial study is not ordered at the same time. Pro tip: check to make sure there is no neuro study tagged to the spine study before reading it. At times, new technologists will send just the spine and not the heads/maxi-face studies. So it’s worth checking your spine study for a concomitant head CT because clinicians do not like walking to multiple reading rooms for interpretations. Check the [spine imaging workflow](#bookmark=id.1v1yuxt) for details. Once all studies completed before 12pm are dictated, you may leave for the afternoon. The junior resident will cover the ED radiographs and the senior resident will cover the MSK cross sectional imaging. Arrange a time to come back or remotely in the evening and read out the junior resident and finish up dictations on all imaging completed before 4:30 PM and all ED imaging completed by 8:00 PM. It is often an advantage to do a readout in the middle of the afternoon as well as the late evening readout.  
3. **Late readout (weekdays):** The radiology department has committed to providing final faculty interpretations for only ED studies (radiographs and cross sectional) completed before 9:00 PM weekdays and 8:00 PM weekends. Please note: Not for inpatient or outpatient studies. Each evening an attending or fellow is assigned to this late read out. Attendings cover M-W. Fellows cover Thursday and Friday nights during your call week and occasional non-call weeks. You will read out the junior resident, providing a final report for all ED exams completed before 9:00 PM. On Saturdays and Sundays when you’re on call, you will read out with the junior resident and complete all ED exams up until 8:00 PM.   
4. **Faculty backup:** A faculty member is assigned as a backup if you have questions, need an urgent 2nd opinion on an imaging study or need help doing an interventional procedure.  Faculty will always come in to assist on the rare spine or biopsy procedures.  
5. You may get paged to cover joint aspirations after hours including at night or over the weekend. Please refer to the section on [setting up joint aspirations on call](#appendix-f:-setting-up-joint-aspirations-on-call) for information about how to do this.

# Fellow Scheduling and Time Off Requests {#fellow-scheduling-and-time-off-requests}

## **Clinical Schedule:** {#clinical-schedule:}

MSK uses Qgenda for scheduling and to request time off. You can access the schedule online or as an app on your phone. You can also sync your personal schedule with your Outlook or Google calendar for convenient access. 

In general, you will be scheduled to one clinical service for a week at a time but there are many exceptions to this and later in the year, you will move around more during the week.

## 

## **Academic Time:** {#academic-time:}

1. Academic time varies based on the overall schedule and whether any fellows are off service.  
2. Anyone on academic must be available on pager and remain local in case they need to be called in for an emergency—this is a hospital-wide policy.  
3. Academic time cannot be used for interviewing for jobs out of town. Likewise, do not schedule flights to depart during an academic afternoon.  
4. There is no elective block. If you anticipate wanting a week or two in the second half of the year to rotate on non-MSK services (e.g. breast), you will need to work with other fellows well in advance (like 4-6 months) to schedule academic time in blocks (precluding any other fellow having academic time or vacation that week).  
5. Acad time is used for scholarly activities, conference preparation, writing, meetings. Not to be used as a “day off” or “sleeping in”. If no scholarly activities then we will assign you to clinical duties. If wanting to do a few days in breast or other rotation this should be planned for the second half of the year and well in advance. Please let the administrative assistant and section chief know by end of January.  
   

## **Call schedule:** {#call-schedule:}

During fellowship orientation you’ll get a copy of the call schedule for the year with call weeks marked out for Fellow A, B, C, D, and E. Every effort has been made to have these call tracks be as equivalent as possible in terms of holiday coverage and other parameters. Review the sheet and discuss with your co-fellows who will take which call track and submit it to Dr. Lee and the MSK admin by July 25th. You will also need to decide on one fellow who will stay on service the last week of June to help cover contrast and this can be a part of deciding who takes what call track and first choice of conference. 

## **Time Off Requests:** {#time-off-requests:}

1. All requests for time off (vacation and meetings) must be entered into QGenda prior to the quarterly deadline. The section admin will send a reminder when the deadline is getting close. **Pro tip**: Plan ahead.  
2. In general, only one fellow is allowed off the schedule at a time with the following exceptions:  
   1. Second absence approved by fellowship director and let the MSK Admin know. We have relaxed this rule since and have allowed up to two fellows off at a time but shouldn’t be recurring consecutive days or weeks at a time.  
   2. RSNA meeting week; 2-3 fellows can go Mon-Tue and 2-3 fellows can go Wed-Fri, depending on staffing.  
   3. Other major meetings (SSR, ARRS, etc.): Up to two fellows can go if they have submitted a scientific abstract for presentation. We have encouraged up to 3 fellows to go to SSR as long as they submitted a podium presentation.  
   4. Holidays: 2 or 3 fellows may take off Christmas week and the other two or three may take off New Year’s week. You must use your vacation days. Christmas Eve, Christmas Day and New Year’s Day are holidays so only the call team will work those days. **New Year’s Eve is not a holiday so two-three fellows will need to be on service that day.** Clinical services are limited and typically only one MSK attending is on service but this day is not a holiday for clinical fellows.   
   5. Up to 4 fellows can take terminal vacation the last five weekdays of June but one fellow must remain to cover WIMR contrast.  
3. If you see in Qgenda that you are the second fellow requesting the day off, you must send an email to Dr. Ross and Natalie Roisum and wait for approval before committing to the time off including buying airline tickets. Having a second fellow off the schedule must be approved by the Fellowship Director.  
4. Fellows cannot take vacation during the following weeks: major meeting weeks including ISS, RSNA, SSR and ARRS; Spring Break weeks for Madison and Middleton schools.   
5. In the event of the death of an immediate family member (grandparents, parents, uncle, aunt, or spouse), you are entitled to take up to three paid clinic days off service for bereavement leave.  
6. As a courtesy to your co-fellows, do not request more days off than you have vacation days as a way to “stake your claim” on certain days.  
7. You must use vacation days for interviewing (i.e. sick leave and academic days are not to be used for interviewing).  
8. **Pro tip**: Spreading out your vacation days is a good idea rather than trying to fit them all in towards the end of the fellowship year. Otherwise, you may not get all your requested days off. Planning ahead helps.  
9. Please note that since you are academic staff you can get paid out for any unused vacation. A full day is 8 hours. Your monthly salary will be broken down to an hourly rate and paid out according to how many vacation hours are leftover.

## **Meeting Attendance Policies:** {#meeting-attendance-policies:}

1. You are allowed up to 5 days of time off the schedule for Meeting Presenting time, i.e. attending meetings where you have an accepted project, and 5 days for Meeting Attending, attending meetings without the obligation to present a project.  
2. Like any time off request, you must enter meeting time into QGenda prior to each quarterly deadline. Please do this as far in advance as possible.   
3. Irrespective of how many projects a fellow completes and how many opportunities a fellow has to present at meetings, understand that there is no guarantee that a fellow can use more days than the Department policy allows (total of 10 meeting days). Vacation days may be used to attend meetings as well, respecting the standard limitations for number of fellows off on the schedule.  
4. If you’re thinking about attending a meeting virtually instead of in-person, please get approval prior to committing to the meeting. 

## **Schedule changes and last minute requests:** {#schedule-changes-and-last-minute-requests:}

1. If you need days off after the schedule has already been made, please first check to see if you can trade with another fellow to have them come off academic to cover your clinical service and then pay them back later by giving up one of your academic days. If you’re already academic, those days can be converted to vacation if you need to fly out of town.  
2. If there is no other fellow who can sub for you, then contact the attending(s) for the services that you need to miss, let them know the reason for your absence and ask if it’s okay if you leave the service without a fellow. This is completely appropriate for things like last minute job interviews or family emergencies, and the vast majority of the time the answer will be yes, but on occasion, some other accommodation may be needed.   
3. Once you get this cleared, email the MSK Administrative Assistant with the changes as well as the affected faculty, fellows, and Drs. Lee and Ross.  
4. If you are taking a sick day and we pull a fellow from academic then you will need to repay said fellow for their lost academic time.

# Fellowship Requirements {#fellowship-requirements}

## **Research** {#research}

Each fellow is expected to participate in one research project during the fellowship year.  The department will pay the expenses for attending a meeting to make a scientific presentation within the expense reimbursement guidelines that you will receive from the Department Administrator. Please review the list of research projects and discuss with respective faculty early (July) because abstract deadlines are usually in September. You will need to coordinate with the other fellows who will submit to which meeting. The SSR, ARRS, AUR, ESSR and AIUM are all typical meetings for fellow research presentations. **No more than two fellows** may attend each of these meetings so you will need to decide (in conjunction with your faculty advisor) early on who will submit where. Of note: SSR \- The faculty member that is listed on the abstract must be in attendance at the SSR.  Please confirm your project and targeted meeting with the Fellowship Director by **July 31st**. You will have the opportunity to present your research to the Section for feedback during a GCC. These typically occur in February ahead of the March-April conferences. Please coordinate a time with the MSK Admin Assistant to find a date to present your research in lieu of GCC.

Mandatory submission to the Zachary Clark Research Symposium

Later in the year, you will have the opportunity to present your research at the annual **Zachary Clark Resident Research Symposium**. The symposium is typically held in Madison on Saturday morning from 8am-12pm in the month of May. More details to follow so you can save the date\! All fellows and residents from the Department are required to submit their research projects since the Dept funds the travel to conferences.

## **WIMR (Wisconsin Institutes for Medical Research) Contrast Coverage** {#wimr-(wisconsin-institutes-for-medical-research)-contrast-coverage}

MSK fellows will be assigned to cover the Department’s research scanners several times per month in case there is an MR or CT contrast reaction. We have little leeway in the WIMR coverage days that are assigned to MSK. Fortunately, the residents in the PET reading room will cover the majority of the day and the fellows will only need to cover during the short periods of time when contrasted scans are scheduled during resident conferences or other times the residents are unavailable. Thankfully, the volume of scans is low and these scan patients are usually volunteers so contrast reactions are rare.  There is a study room set up with a PC linked to the network and a PACS workstation with dictation capability. Please check with the Nuclear Medicine Manager at 265-8734 and/or the WIMR Imaging Scheduler at 263-7098 prior to your assignment to see what times the contrast studies are scheduled and when you may need to be available. New since 2022, most of the time you can work clinically as assigned and be pager ready for any contrast reactions that may occur.

Contrast coverage at the WIMR is important and needs to be covered daily by all non-accredited UW fellows except for the Friday after Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year’s holiday weeks and the first week of July for orientation. **At least one MSK fellow** must work through the last weekday of June to cover one or two of the MSK assigned WIMR contrast coverage days. This can be a tradeoff for attending a preferred conference such as SSR or a preferred vacation. Please see [Appendix D: WIMR Contrast Coverage Guidelines](#appendix-d:-wimr-contrast-coverage-guidelines) for more details. Please let the Fellowship Director know which fellow will be staying through the last week of June.

You will receive much more information about Meriter moonlighting during orientation. # Appendix D: WIMR Contrast Coverage Guidelines {#appendix-d:-wimr-contrast-coverage-guidelines}

• On pre-determined days, fellows will be expected to spend time in WIMR, to be available to monitor contrast reactions for research and clinical studies performed in MRI, CT, PET/CT and PET/MR scanners at WIMR, as well as for research scans performed on UW MR7 located at the Department of Human Oncology. Fortunately, the residents in the PET reading room will cover the majority of the day and the fellows will only need to cover during the short periods of time when contrasted scans are scheduled during resident conferences or other times the residents are unavailable. Most of the time fellows can remain on their clinical service and just be available by pager. But be sure to check in with the front desk to get an overview of the schedule and if/when you’ll need to be onsite at WIMR. When you’re not needed at WIMR, you can return to your clinical assignment (if assigned) or work on your academic projects if assigned to academic time. Be sure to notify your staff if you are cross covering at WIMR while on a clinical rotation. 

• Fellows will receive a reminder notification via email 48-72 hours prior to their scheduled WIMR contrast coverage day. This email will include the currently scheduled procedures that require contrast injections. This is a tentative schedule subject to changes and add-ons. Check at the WIMR front desk for the current schedule on the day of coverage. Contrast procedures may be scheduled from 8:00 AM until 5:00 PM. In specific cases, if a contrast procedure is to be scheduled at 7:30 AM, later cases on that day should be scheduled such that the fellow can leave no later than 4:30 PM.

• The WIMR contrast coverage schedule is found at [https://www.radiology.wisc.edu](https://www.radiology.wisc.edu) \>  
Intranet \> Schedules \> Clinical Schedule \> WIMR Contrast.

• If fellows are scheduled to cover WIMR contrast injections and a conflict arises, it is the fellow’s responsibility to trade with another fellow who is available. The fellows or their administrative assistant may make these changes. If the fellow cannot find another fellow to trade with, they should notify their Section Chief or Fellowship Director to resolve this issue.

• Please notify Chris Jaskowiak, [CJaskowiak@uwhealth.org](mailto:CJaskowiak@uwhealth.org) or 265-8734, of any schedule changes and she will update the calendar. If Chris is unavailable, you may contact Marne Vanderpas, PET Technologist, at [MVanderpas@uwhealth.org](mailto:MVanderpas@uwhealth.org) or 265-8732.

• A designated work area for the fellows has been established in WIMR room 1220, the IMAC- Image Analysis Core room. Cell phone reception currently is limited; however, pagers do work. The phone number in room 1220 is 263-8888. Please be aware that paging and cell phone reception is limited in the PET/CT and PET/MR suites. The PET Fellows are usually in the WIMR PET Reading Room (263-1252)

• Contrast scheduling will occur throughout the year, except for the Friday after Thanksgiving, the week between Christmas and New Year’s, and the first week in July. Contrast scheduling will continue during meeting weeks as long as there are a sufficient number of fellows available with academic days.

• Contrast Reaction Kits and Crash Carts are located in the CT control room (1241) and the PET/CT hallway (B1248). All fellows are expected to be up to date on the treatment of contrast reactions and should familiarize themselves with the location and contents of the Contrast Reaction Kits. Radiology HR issues badge access to these areas. Please let Chris Jaskowiak know if you do not receive access clearance.

• For DHO (MR7) MRI, the contrast reaction tray is located on the bottom shelf of the cabinet directly behind the scanner console in the control room. A “Basic Life Support” cart is located in the storage closet (K4/B31) across from the MRI suite. A full “Crash Cart” can be found near the nurse’s station in L7/B20. Emergency telephone and paging instructions are on the wall behind the scanner console.

• To call a Blue Cart have a member of the response team, call 262-0000. The hospital code team will respond. In addition, please also call 911\. The Madison Fire Department will respond.

• If you have any questions or concerns regarding the WIMR contrast schedule please contact Chris Jaskowiak at 265-8734, pager 8546, email [CJaskowiak@uwhealth.org](mailto:CJaskowiak@uwhealth.org), or Dr. Greg Avey (pager 2680).

# Appendix E: Absence Request Self-Service; Employee Quick Reference Guide  {#appendix-e:-absence-request-self-service;-employee-quick-reference-guide}

Fellows will be paid out any remaining balances at the end of their fellowship or if they were  
to resign prior to the end date. This would include:

• Personal Holiday: Any hours unused, this is not prorated.  
• Legal Holiday: any unused and earned floating legal holidays (earned \=  
worked or was in pay status the day before or the day after the LH)  
• Vacation: any unused and earned (if they leave prior to the end of the fiscal  
year this will be prorated to the amount they earned from 7/1/24 to the date of  
resignation)

**ABSENCE REQUEST SELF-SERVICE**  
**EMPLOYEE QUICK REFERENCE GUIDE**  
This employee guide will assist you with the absence request self-service process. If you have any questions, please contact our Payroll & Benefits Specialist, Nancy Apfelbeck, at [napfelbeck@wisc.edu](mailto:napfelbeck@wisc.edu), 608-265-9048, or your MSK admins. 

**LEGAL HOLIDAYS:**

* Legal holidays will automatically load based on FTE if 1.0 FTE. Employees do not need to enter legal holidays if the hours are correct.  
* If employee is less than 1.0 FTE, the employee will receive a prorated amount based on HOURS PAID (worked and paid leave) in the pay period.   
* If an employee needs to void or change the number of hours worked for a legal holiday, contact your payroll representative.  
* If employee requests a floating holiday, the employee must manually enter the request as “Legal Holiday”.

**SUBMISSION OF LEAVE REPORTS:**

* Absence requests and approvals are due by the fifth of each month per leave reporting policies. Failure to submit leave reports, per Section VIII(a) of the Sick Leave Policy, impacts an employee’s sick leave.   
* If an employee submits a leave report online but the report is not approved by the primary and/or backup approvers, even if no leave was taken, the employee’s leave report will count as missing and subject to sick leave reduction as noted above.

Section VIII(a) of the Sick Leave Policy

| *“a. Any faculty, academic staff, or limited appointee who fails to file a report on leave usage as required by UW-Madison policy in one or more months of any year shall not be permitted to accrue sick leave for that year in an amount exceeding the cap established by Wis. Stat. 40.05(04)bp)1 (i.e., 8.5 days if annual-basis or 6/4 days if academic year-basis). The cap may be blended if the employee has both an academic year and annual basis appointment during the same fiscal year. Per Section XI.b. and c. of the Sick Leave Policy, leave reports must be approved whether submitted via paper or electronic by the “employee’s department chair, director, supervisor, or designee must also sign the monthly leave report.”* |
| :---- |

**REFERENCE LEAVE REQUESTS:**

**EXAMPLE \#1:**  
If absence request includes days from two different weeks/months, employee needs to enter three separate absence requests \- one for each week/month.

**EXAMPLE \#2:**  
If absence request is for August 23 and 24, and the employee wants to use two different types of leave, such as vacation and personal holiday, the employee will need to enter TWO separate absence requests \- one for each type of leave. If leave crosses weekends, then employee would need to submit separate requests for the following week as well.

* Vacation \- August 23  
* Personal Holiday \- August 24 

# Appendix F: Setting up joint aspirations on call {#appendix-f:-setting-up-joint-aspirations-on-call}

As you start to take first call shifts through the remainder of the year, you'll want to know how to handle pages for joint aspirations which you may receive after hours. On-call joint aspirations are part of what we cover when we're on call in adult patients (18 years or older). Pediatric aspirations are done by pediatric radiology. If you get a page for a peds patient please kindly refer them to the on-call radiology resident. 

Additionally, we do not offer after hours aspirations at EMH. If one is requested, options are to transfer the patient to UW for the procedure or to defer until business hours. 

To start with you'll want to gather all the standard information that you would for any patient to make sure the procedure is feasible and appropriate:

\-Patient name/MRN  
\-Brief history  
\-Is the patient consentable? Moveable?  
\-Anticoagulation? (not a contraindication but good to know)  
\-Specific joint if not clear. (For example, shoulder could be bursa, GH joint, or AC joint).  
\-Whether there has been any prior imaging of the area or any prior procedures at this site

You'll also want to make sure that the referring service puts in orders for the aspiration and any labs that they want.

If you decide that the procedure is appropriate to do, decide what modality you want (fluoroscopy or ultrasound).

For fluoroscopy, you'll contact the DR techs at pager 7941 or charge phone 608-576-5728. They will either arrange to have a DR tech cover the procedure or they will contact the IR tech to arrange coverage.

For ultrasound, there is always someone on site, so you can call the ultrasound QB number at 262-5279.

If you'll need conscious sedation, you can also page the radiology nurse at "RADIOLOGY NURSE/NEURO" in the paging system or the fluoro tech can help you get in touch with them. But this is rare.

Your back up call attending is always a resource for you at any step in this process. You should have a low threshold to touch base with them regarding if the procedure should be done, tips for procedure success, and any logistic issues you have along the way.
